title: fix(cli): reject --gateway combined with --node in approvals commands
body:
Closes #176200

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw approvals` commands silently drop a `--node <node>` target when `--gateway` is also passed, operating on the gateway approval policy instead — including security-relevant writes such as `allowlist add` and `set`.

## User Impact

User impact: passing both `--gateway` and `--node <node>` to an approvals command now fails immediately with `Pass only one of --gateway or --node.` instead of silently mutating the wrong policy target and exiting 0.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveTargetNodeId` in `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.ts` returned `null` whenever `--gateway` was set, so the `--node` value was never resolved and `loadSnapshotTarget` routed the whole command to the gateway. The CLI already rejects conflicting target flags elsewhere (capability commands reject `--local --gateway` with the same "Pass only one of ..." wording), so this aligns approvals commands with the established convention.

## Evidence

**Real shipped-CLI behavior** (source checkout, isolated fixture state; `logging.consoleStyle=json`):

```
$ openclaw approvals get --gateway --node macbook
exit 1
stderr: {"level":"error","message":"Pass only one of --gateway or --node."}

$ openclaw approvals allowlist add /usr/bin/uname --gateway --node macbook
exit 1
stderr: {"level":"error","message":"Pass only one of --gateway or --node."}

$ openclaw approvals get --gateway        # control: single target
exit 1
stderr: {"level":"error","message":"gateway exec.approvals.get requires credentials before opening a websocket"}
```

The conflict commands exit non-zero with the rejection message before any policy access; the single-target control passes the conflict check and fails later at gateway auth, confirming the fix is scoped to the conflicting pair.

**New process-level regression** `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.process.test.ts` runs the actual CLI entry (`src/entry.ts`) as a child process and asserts the same exit codes and output; `pnpm test src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 3/3.

**Unit regressions** in `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts` (`get` and `allowlist add`) assert rejection, the message, and no gateway RPC; the full file passes 27/27. Red/green: both new unit tests fail on the pre-fix code.

**Static checks:** `run-tsgo.mjs -p src/cli/tsconfig.json` clean; `run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <files>` clean; `oxfmt --check` clean.

The `autoreview` skill helper was not run: the `codex` CLI is not installed in this environment.


### Maintainer validation

Production delta: **+5 lines** (+8/−3), three changed files. The small increase rejects an ambiguous approval-policy target at the existing resolver before reads or writes. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0/P1 findings on `0036a8407b172f3536001ae01cd33b3c04263b0b`.

Exact-head CI run [39128611478](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39128611478) passed, including lint, types and the test owners. CI measured the approval suite at **27 passed, 2.60s Vitest / 4.02s wrapper wall time**, and the CLI process suite at **3 passed, 7.91s Vitest / 9.45s wrapper wall time**. The process suite exercises actual CLI registration and error output; the cheaper suite checks the absence of policy RPCs. No local contributor-code execution or fresh local test measurement is claimed.
